dominant_strengths: Faithful macOS Finder recreation with accurate sidebar grouping, traffic lights, toolbar density, and authentic chrome typography
Pastel-tinted file icons (red PDFs, yellow code, green spreadsheet) provide clean color-coded scanning without breaking neutrality
Spatial rhythm of the icon grid is even, with consistent gutters and well-balanced sidebar-to-content ratio
dominant_weaknesses: It is essentially a Finder clone—zero conceptual invention, no novel interaction or organizational metaphor beyond Apple's defaults
Two-line filename wrapping (design-system.pdf, meeting-recording.mp4) creates uneven baseline rows and visual noise in the grid
Emotional and reflective payoff is thin; nothing rewards a second look or signals a designer's point of view
fix_priorities: Introduce a distinctive POV—custom file previews, semantic grouping, or a novel navigation affordance—to escape pure mimicry
Stabilize filename truncation to single-line with ellipsis to preserve grid baseline alignment
Tighten icon color saturation parity so PDF red doesn't overpower the softer pastel set
rationale.norman_balance: Strong behavioral familiarity and decent visceral polish, but reflective depth is near zero because it copies rather than reinterprets.
rationale.intent_fit: It clearly executes a file-browser, but as 'original' work it leans almost entirely on Finder's existing language.
